text.card: A star 54 parsecs away, 154 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 3,221 times the Sun's luminosity at 3,508 K, so 153.871 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 112122: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Beta Gruis
quotes.card: Beta Gruis, formally named Tiaki, is the second brightest star in the southern constellation of Grus.
quotes.introduction: It was once considered the rear star in the tail of the constellation of the (Southern) Fish, Piscis Austrinus: it, with Alpha, Delta, Theta, Iota, and Lambda Gruis, belonged to Piscis Austrinus in medieval Arabic astronomy.
